annotations.text: POST-MVP — rounds drawn before their slice is the work. The four canonical canvases and designs/canonical are the MVP baseline implementation reads from; this tree is where a later round is drawn, reviewed and held until its slice becomes current, at which point its boards move across to canonical as a reviewed round. Same design system, same flow grammar, same build: boards render from design/components, the page opens with a generated flow map, and graph.json binds each orange number to its outcomes. Nothing implementation needs is ever only here.

CHANGE HISTORIES — would-like #2, drawn 2026-09-22. Two kinds of history, one door rule. A post, a comment and a profile each open a chronicle: every version WHOLE, newest first, the current one marked, never a diff — the store keeps complete states, and on L1 every edit signs a full new record of its own. A removed version keeps its row and wears the mark. A stance is a history too: the bundle IS the list of records ever cast from one node to another, and the timeline says in plain words what the standing adds up to, because a sum that clips hides the conviction behind it. The doors follow one law — authoring doors are faces and fields, HISTORY DOORS ARE READOUTS: the stance face on a card is untouched, the value at a row's end opens the timeline, and the pad's Current opinion line carries the only new ink. Timelines are public to everyone, signed out included; the gates stay on acting.

CHATS — would-like #3, drawn and revised 2026-09-23. The one surface where CoGra takes messenger convention whole: a list of your chats with a floating New chat (the product's first FAB), bubbles with your own on the right, a live field at the foot. Underneath, a chat is the proposal primitive in messenger clothes — nothing here may look like a proposal. The send arrow IS the seal: tapping it signs the message in your name, and holding it opens what you sign. Each message is plaintext or encrypted by the lock beside the field — plaintext by default, sticky per chat, the state shown by the lock's fill — and every encrypted message wears a quiet lock; previews and bubbles show the words wherever you hold the key. Rows keep the ages ladder, the thread prints the clock and divides the days. The page has two faces that swap both ways: your chats, and all chats — the ordinary rank narrowed to chats, no second algorithm, your own chats hidden by default. Long-press is the second gesture: a row for the chat's options, a bubble for the message's acts. Messages never edit. The chat's detail surface, behind the thread's header, is drawn in the rows below.

CHAT DETAILS — round B1 of the chats work, drawn 2026-09-23. What the thread's header and the row menu open: a messenger's group info through CoGra's grammar. The chat's face, name and words at the top, and its own OPINION control leading the actions row (the profile header's precedent), with Edit chat beside it wherever the governance map lets the reader propose a change. Media, then OPEN DECISIONS — where an act that needs more voices than its actor's waits; empty here, filled in round B2. Search rides the thread's header, beside the details door, on every thread. The members wear their roles, and for a member each role word is a door to the role change; a Collective can be a member; an invited person who has not joined yet is marked, and NO ROW EVER SHOWS PRESENCE. Mute silences push only and lives here and on the row menu. Leave is unilateral, with an optional parting reason that stands in the chat's history. The metadata grows in whole versions like a post's — its successions — and the edit history shows them newest first with who joined, left and was invited between them, never inside them, and every member may start a version's removal — a chat has no author. The edit's seal counts three things signed together: the change, its link to the chat, and the proposer's own opinion for it. Chats are public, so a reader outside gets the same page minus the member's acts, with the join on the actions row. The multi-voice faces behind Add people, the role change, a version's removal and the change that waits for more voices are the governance rows below.

CHATS GOVERNANCE — round B2 of the chats work, drawn 2026-09-23 and revised on jakob's canvas review 2026-09-24. The multi-voice acts, in messenger clothes: nothing here may look like a proposal. An act the actor's own say settles is INSTANT — a seal counting three things signed together, the change, its link and their own opinion for it. An act that needs more voices becomes a QUIET CARD IN THE THREAD at the moment it was proposed: a plain sentence, Disagree and Agree, and a count of the PEOPLE who agree — 2 of 5 so far. Both are real votes: every threshold reads what was cast, so a disagreement counts, and a decision whose against side crosses first FAILS for good — its outcome line says what stayed, as a passed one says what changed. No vote signs on a bare tap: each opens a small seal that says the vote in one sentence. A card's words open the DECISION WHOLE — what would change in full, the new picture included; every vote, who and which way; and your own, with Disagree instead and Take back your vote. The same decisions stand as rows under Open decisions on the details. THE COUNT CONVENTION, for review: cards count people and never show weight; the tally underneath is weighted by role, and the decision page shows both directions, with the arithmetic in geek mode. Nothing expires. Inviting is the inviter's own act, never a decision: a picker, then a seal counting one invitation per person. Joining is always the joiner's own record, one seal for three routes — open, invited, approved; an approval never joins anyone by itself. A request shows as a card the approver meets in the thread, with Approve. Role words open a sheet of the three roles; a version's removal is the chat's decision, and a removed version keeps its row under the chat's own mark.

CHATS INTEGRATION — round B3, drawn 2026-09-24, the round that closes the chats work. What a chat owes the rest of the product, and what the rest owes a chat. REACTIONS are the opinions already cast on a message: the faces aggregated with a count under the bubble, WhatsApp's shape, no new record and no emoji system; a tap opens Opinions on this. The foot takes a REPLY'S QUOTE, and a landed reply carries it. VOICE NOTES join as a chat-scale media kind: the mic stands where the arrow stands while the field is empty, tap to record, and the foot becomes the recording's controls — Describe, delete, the lock, pause (which flips to Keep recording and extends the note) and send; no hidden gesture ever signs. Tapping a trace opens the message's opinions, and Give your opinion opens the pad. AN ENCRYPTED MESSAGE ENCRYPTS ITS ATTACHMENTS on the device: a keyed reader sees the media with the quiet lock; a no-key reader gets a reserved tile with the lock and one friendly sentence — no expand to bytes, because cipher pixels are nothing, and no server path can ever process such a blob. A message PENDING shows whole, Still settling before its clock; one that expires leaves every reader's view and tells its author calmly. A REMOVED message is a mark where the bubble stood, and the author's removal never reads like the platform's. EVERY SHARE opens Send to a chat, the OS share inside it, and the sent post lands as a message citing it. The chat and the message become FEED CARDS; a chat is a SEARCH RESULT that opens its read surface for anyone; a message is SAVED like a comment. THREE NOTIFICATION KINDS — an invitation, a request awaiting you, your request approved — and push gains chat messages, which never write bell rows. ASK TO JOIN and INVITING each take an optional message, and an invited reader's explorer row says You're invited. EVERY SEAL THAT JOINS OR ASKS lets you set your opinion on the chat on the real pad. And every board here mounts the real masters — the feed cards are the feed's own card, ⋮ and action row included.

MONEY · The CGT figure (item 11, system). One shape for every amount: two decimals, thousands grouped, the mark trailing where the unit word would sit. Dust is '< 0.01' — never 0.00, a shown number that lies — exact value one layer down; zero is '0', plainly (a new member's true state). Amounts are never negative: a minus is an OUTFLOW on a history line; positive inflows opt into '+'. No colour on direction — the system has no green, and error-colouring spending would call it a failure. The unit is the MARK everywhere (jakob 2026-08-31: the word 'CGT' repeated everywhere doesn't look nice); the word appears once — the wallet's balance headline, mark and word adjacent, its '?' explaining both as CoGra's own money. The mark is the BRAND MARK on the coin (jakob 2026-08-31, round 2): cogra-mark.svg verbatim, knocked out monochrome in the on-primary on the primary disc. Round 1's lone C read as any game's coin; CG letters, a CG interlock, and c+dot were drawn and rejected against it. The wallet's surfaces are item 12; pending amounts wait for it.

WALLET (item 12, jakob's rulings 2026-08-31, grounded in a doc audit + the admission-money-on-Liquid decision). The balance headline is the ONE surface spelling CGT (mark + word + the What-is-CGT '?'), with the ≈ L-BTC VALUE line read from the public CGT–L-BTC market (the protocol's own ladder, live from genesis) — an estimate, never a promise, hidden at zero. NO free-form send (tipping IS the user-to-user send; off-graph moves are any Liquid tool's job) and NO cash-out surface. HISTORY: one stream, newest first — payouts, tips in and out, campaign money — every line opening what paid it; an unlanded payout wears Still settling (the pending look item 11 deferred here); direction by sign and words, never colour. CAMPAIGNS: money view only (deposit, escrow, window, settles-as-public-record); the campaign card will click through to a details page when one exists. THE RAIL KEY IS BORN LAZILY at first wallet open (docs: ledger.md Keys) — no new recovery code, the key joins the one container under the one code ('Your wallet key' ?); the ceremony's single signed act is publishing the payout address. The address renders WHOLE, mono, never truncated (checking it is the point); changing it is a seal — parallel Registration, newest wins, every prior address stays witnessed. Key-absent: balance and history stay readable (public chain), signing needs the key — restore-first. Guest: the honest explanation + the join prompt. Applicant: the wallet opens with membership — nothing locked, nothing yet to show. ROUND 2 (jakob, same day — 'make it sexy', direction A blessed WITH the gradient): the balance is a TROPHY — the hero rides THE BRAND WASH (--surface-hero, the one decorative gradient surface, first of its kind; jakob: the product reads 'basic' next to Instagram's brand feel, this is the start of fixing that) with the brand coin GHOSTED oversized into the corner, display-size figure, and the real recent-earnings delta chip. Progress: the EARNED BARS — every bar a real settlement, tappable, latest wears primary (honest decoration; nothing modeled). History rows are IDENTITY ROWS: the disc is who the money moved with (tipper's face, campaign's cover, glyph), wearing the direction badge; the amount stays uncoloured. THE CAMPAIGN MOVED TO ITS OWN SUBPAGE (Wallet · your campaign — committing 12,500 is a big deal): money facts + its rail history; the main page keeps one entry row. The address lives in a CARD with copy + Change (compact at rest, captioned on the zero state and seals). Zero-state wording is PATH-TRUE: campaigns pay when paths between crowd and target run through you; posting is how paths start, not a guarantee. Key notice LEADS the key-absent board, inset like every card. Guest prompt centered; applicant told plainly: come back after approval — earnings can't land until the address exists. ROUND 3 (jakob, same day): AT REST THE ADDRESS IS ONE LINE, high on the page (PayoutAddressRow — the one place the address may shorten, head…tail; it is an entry point, and the full card with copy/Change/caption is one tap away; the never-truncate rule holds on every checking surface — the card, the seals, the zero state where the full card sits high). THE CAMPAIGN SECTION IS GONE from the main page: campaign money is ORDINARY HISTORY — three kinds: escrow out at creation, top-up out, return in when the payout wasn't full — and the wallet keeps only the CAMPAIGNS DOOR to the campaigns page ('Wallet · campaigns'): Start a campaign, the Yours/You-took-part segments, Open with amounts, Past with outcomes; a listed campaign opens the money subpage ('Wallet · your campaign'). THE MOMENT SCREENS WEAR THE WASH (WashCard — the wash + ghost coin extracted as one master; at most one per screen): first open, guest, and applicant are a person's first look at the money side and must not read as settings.

THE WALLET'S ? CONTENTS — the two texts the wallet's ? opens, in canonical's plain dialog ('The ? dialog' board). The copy, verbatim:

WALLET BALANCE · 'What is CGT?': CGT is CoGra's own money. Advertisers fund campaigns with it, and it pays the people whose posts and stances carried real reach — the small coin always means CGT. / It's yours the moment it lands: earnings are paid straight to you, held by your key, never by CoGra. Every amount can be traced to what paid it, and the ≈ value reads the public CGT–L-BTC market — it moves with the market and is never a promise.

WALLET SET-UP · 'Your wallet key': Your wallet gets its own key — created on this device, never held by CoGra, restored by the same recovery code as your signing key. One code, both keys. / Publishing your payout address is a signed action. The address is public, payouts and tips land there, and every change to it stays on your public record.
